Schema Validation with Zod →

The Limits of Manual Checks

Three places doing their own ad hoc validation, and what that costs as the API grows.

By now this project has three separate hand-rolled checks, all doing roughly the same job in slightly different ways: createTicket's if (!subject || !description || !customerId) (Lesson 1, Figure 1.8), getTicketById's Number.isNaN(id) guard (Lesson 2, Figure 2.16), and — about to be written for this lesson — the same two problems again for Comment and Tag, plus new ones: is status one of the four values the database actually accepts? Is page a positive number, or could ?page=-1 reach Prisma at all?

Three things go wrong if this keeps scaling by hand:

  • Duplication. Every route re-invents "is this field present, is this id numeric" from scratch, in prose that's easy to phrase inconsistently.
  • No coercion. Number(req.params.id) is a manual conversion step every single handler needs to remember, by hand, before the value is usable.
  • Drift. Nothing stops one controller's error message from reading 'subject and description are required' while another says 'id must be a number' — the shape of a validation failure isn't guaranteed to be consistent even within this one small API.

A schema fixes all three at once: describe once, in one place, what a valid request looks like — field names, types, required-ness, allowed values — and get both the pass/fail check and the coercion from checking against it. That's what Zod is, and what the rest of this topic wires into Express.
